questions.question: Why should a production system generate overlapping temporal windows instead of unrelated frames?
options: Overlapping windows reduce object storage durability requirements.
They share temporal context so identity, scene state, and motion can remain coherent across boundaries.
They remove the need for sequence-level validation.
They guarantee every prompt can be rendered as one continuous shot.
questions.explanation: Shared context across overlapping windows constrains boundary frames and reduces identity, lighting, and motion discontinuities.

questions.question: A preview costs 5 GPU-minutes, a final render costs 20 GPU-minutes, and 60% of previews are approved. What is the expected compute per submitted job?
options: 12 GPU-minutes
17 GPU-minutes
20 GPU-minutes
25 GPU-minutes
questions.explanation: Every request pays 5 preview GPU-minutes and 60% pay 20 final GPU-minutes: 5 + 0.6 x 20 = 17 GPU-minutes.

questions.question: Which component should own durable stage state, retries, and checkpoint references?
options: The browser connection
The CDN edge cache
The job orchestrator backed by a transactional job record
A single long-running accelerator process
questions.explanation: Generation is asynchronous and workers are replaceable. Durable orchestration makes each bounded stage resumable after process or machine loss.

questions.question: Why is prompt-only moderation insufficient for text-to-video generation?
options: Video prompts are always encrypted.
A harmless prompt can still produce an unsafe frame, transition, identity use, or audio sequence.
Prompt moderation consumes more storage than frame moderation.
The storyboard always predicts every generated pixel exactly.
questions.explanation: Safety is temporal: generated behavior can violate policy even when the input text appears allowed, so the plan, windows, and final sequence also need checks.

questions.question: A worker fails while rendering window 7 of an otherwise checkpointed clip. What is the preferred recovery?
options: Restart the entire clip with a new seed.
Publish the first six windows as a successful result.
Resume from the last accepted checkpoint and regenerate the smallest affected window plus overlap.
Skip window 7 and ask the encoder to hide the gap.
questions.explanation: Atomic checkpoints and bounded windows contain retry cost while preserving the approved plan, seed, and continuity context.

questions.question: A candidate improves average visual preference but doubles identity drift for multi-character clips. What should the release decision be?
options: Launch because aggregate preference improved.
Launch only to users who request long clips.
Hold or shadow the candidate until the failing slice meets the identity guardrail.
Remove multi-character clips from evaluation after launch.
questions.explanation: A hard identity or safety guardrail cannot be traded for a better aggregate aesthetic score. The failing slice blocks broader exposure.
